title: Chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy following COVID-19 vaccination: a case report and literature review
case_prompt:
A 67-year-old man presented with progressive tingling and paresthesia in both lower extremities. Seven days before symptom onset, he had received a third dose of the BBIBP-CorV (Sinopharm) COVID-19 vaccine. His medical history included diabetes mellitus treated with metformin and knee arthrosis. He denied recent infections. Over two months, the sensory symptoms ascended, and weakness in the lower extremities progressed to the point of difficulty initiating ambulation. Lumbosacral MRI showed mild bulging of the L5–S1 intervertebral disc. Treatment with gabapentin and physical therapy yielded no improvement, and over the next two months the paresthesia and weakness extended to the upper extremities. 

On neurological examination, cranial nerves were intact. Motor strength (MRC scale) was 5/5 in cervical muscles, 4/5 in deltoids, 4/5 in wrist and finger movements, 3/5 proximal in the lower extremities, and 2/5 distally, with ankle dorsiflexion graded 2/5. Sensory testing revealed impaired position and vibration sense and reduced pin-prick sensation in the upper and distal lower extremities. The patient had action and postural tremor in the arms, gait ataxia, and generalized areflexia. There was no autonomic dysfunction, dysphagia, or incontinence. 

EMG and nerve conduction studies revealed absent compound muscle action potentials in the lower limbs; in the median, ulnar, and radial nerves there was increased distal latency, marked amplitude reduction, slowed conduction velocity, and conduction block, consistent with a demyelinating sensorimotor polyneuropathy.
diagnostic_reasoning:
1. Diabetic neuropathy — “Based on the clinical presentation and EMG-NCV results, we ruled out other possible differential diagnoses, including diabetic neuropathy…”  
2. Diabetic amyotrophy — “Based on the clinical presentation and EMG-NCV results, we ruled out other possible differential diagnoses, including … diabetic amyotrophy…”  
3. Other immune-mediated neuropathies — “Based on the clinical presentation and EMG-NCV results, we ruled out other possible differential diagnoses, including … other immune-mediated neuropathies.”
